metric.why: Some operators and older DCIM dashboards report DCiE rather than PUE. Knowing both prevents misreading a 77 percent DCiE as something other than a 1.3 PUE.
metric.target: A 1.3 PUE and a 77 percent DCiE are the same facility.
metric.formula: (IT equipment energy / total facility energy) x 100
metric.definition: The same measurement as PUE expressed the other way round, IT energy as a percentage of total facility energy.

reading.body:
DCiE, Data Center Infrastructure Efficiency, expresses the same underlying measurement as PUE but the other way round, IT energy as a percentage of total facility energy, so that a 1.3 PUE and a 77 percent DCiE describe the identical facility.

Some operators and older data center infrastructure management dashboards report DCiE rather than PUE, and knowing the relationship between the two prevents a reader from misreading a 77 percent DCiE as some separate, better or worse measurement than a 1.3 PUE, when it is mathematically the same number inverted.

The metric's siblings, PUE, breaker-level load and peak draw, and power density per rack, are grouped under Power efficiency, and the practical use of DCiE is almost entirely translation, converting between whichever of the two figures a given operator happens to publish.
